summary: When someone sells a house without saying more, some attached parts are not part of the sale, like a side gallery, an inner room, or a roof with a high fence around it. Rabbi Yehuda adds that a roof with a doorway shape is not sold either.

chunks.st: One who sells a house
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has not sold the side gallery,
chunks.st: has not sold the gallery,
chunks.stMore: an extension built above or alongside the main building,

words.note: A narrow room built along the outside of the house.

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא פְתוּחָה לְתוֹכוֹ,
chunks.en: even though it opens into the house,
chunks.st: and this is so even if the gallery is attached to the house and opens into it.

chunks.en: and not the room behind it,
chunks.st: Nor has he sold the room behind
chunks.stMore: the house, even if it is accessible only from inside the house.

chunks.st: He has also not sold the roof

chunks.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ מַעֲקֶה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
chunks.en: when it has a fence ten tefachim high around it.
chunks.st: when it has a parapet ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: as such a roof is considered a separate entity and is therefore not included in the sale of the house.

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it has the shape of a doorway,
chunks.st: If the parapet has the form of a doorway,
chunks.stMore: that is, if it consists of two upright posts with a beam crossing over them, then

chunks.st: even if the parapet is not
ten handbreadths high, the roof
is not sold
chunks.stMore: together with the house, unless it is specifically included in the sale.

summary: Someone who sells a house does not sell the pit or cistern with it. Rabbi Akiva and the Sages argue whether the seller, or a different buyer of the pit, must buy a path through the other's land to get to it.

chunks.en: He has not sold the pit,
chunks.st: One who sells a house without specification has sold neither the pit
nor the cistern [dut],

words.note: A tank for water built above the ground.

chunks.en: even though he wrote for him
chunks.st: even if he writes for the buyer in the bill of sale that he is selling him

chunks.explain: That is, everything from the bottom to the top.
chunks.st: the depth and the height
chunks.stMore: of the house, as anything that is not part of the house, like pits and cisterns, must be explicitly mentioned in the contract or else they remain in the seller’s possession.

chunks.en: And the seller must buy himself a path to them.
chunks.st: And therefore the seller must purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain to reach whatever remains his, because he has sold the area of the house along with the house itself, and he no longer has permission to walk there. This is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: The seller need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain, as this is certainly included in what he has withheld for himself from the sale.

chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva concedes

chunks.en: that when he said to him, except for these,
chunks.st: that when the seller says to the buyer in the bill of sale: I am selling you this house apart from the pit and the cistern,

chunks.en: he does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: he need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain. Since the seller unnecessarily emphasized that the pit and the cistern are not included in the sale, he presumably intended to reserve for himself the right of access to them.

chunks.en: If he sold them to someone else,
chunks.st: If the seller kept the house, but sold the pit and the cistern to another,
Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: the buyer does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: The buyer need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the seller’s domain to reach what he has bought.

chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he needs to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: He must purchase for himself a path through the seller’s domain.

summary: Someone who sells a house sells the things that are fixed to it, like the door, but not the things that can be carried away, like the key. If he says he is selling the house and everything in it, then all of it is sold.

chunks.st: One who sells a house has, as part of the sale,
sold also the door,
but not the key.

chunks.en: He has sold the mortar that is fixed in place,
chunks.st: He has sold the mortar that is fixed in the ground,

words.note: A heavy bowl for crushing grain.

chunks.en: but not one that can be moved.
chunks.st: but not the portable one.

chunks.en: He has sold the bottom millstone,
chunks.st: He has sold the immovable lower millstone [ha’itzterobil],
but not the portable upper stone [hakelet],
chunks.stMore: the funnel into which one pours the grain to be ground.

chunks.st: And he has sold neither the oven
nor the double stove, as they are deemed movable.
When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it, and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold as part of the sale of the house.

summary: Someone who sells a courtyard sells the houses and pits in it, but not the things that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Either way, he does not sell a bathhouse or olive press there, and Rabbi Eliezer says he sells only the open space.

chunks.st: One who sells a courtyard
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.st: has sold with it the houses,
pits, ditches, and caves found in the courtyard,

chunks.en: but not the things that can be moved.
chunks.st: but he has not sold the movable property.
When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold
chunks.stMore: along with the courtyard, even the movable property.

chunks.st: Both in this case, where he executes the sale without specification, and in that
chunks.stMore: case, where he adds the phrase that includes the movable property,

chunks.en: he has not sold the bathhouse
chunks.st: he has not sold the bathhouse,

chunks.en: and not the olive press inside it.
chunks.st: nor has he sold the olive press that is in
chunks.stMore: the courtyard, as each is an entity with a discrete purpose and not an integral part of the courtyard.

chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who sells a courtyard
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.he: לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא אֲוִירָהּ שֶׁל חָצֵר:
chunks.en: has sold only the open space of the courtyard.
chunks.st: has sold only the airspace, i.e., the open space, of the courtyard,
chunks.stMore: but nothing found in the courtyard, not even the houses.

summary: Someone who sells an olive press sells the parts that are fixed in place, but not the parts that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Rabbi Eliezer says the big pressing beam is sold too.

chunks.en: Someone who sells an olive press
chunks.st: One who sells an olive press
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.st: has sold with it the yam

words.note: The stone where the olives are put to be crushed.

chunks.en: and the crushing stone and the posts.
chunks.st: and the memel and the betulot, the immovable elements of the olive press.

words.note: The stone that crushes the olives.
Wooden posts that hold up the beam.

chunks.en: But he has not sold the boards,
chunks.st: But he has not sold with it the avirim

words.note: Heavy boards put on top of the olives.

chunks.explain: These are parts of the press that can be moved.
chunks.st: and the galgal and the kora, the movable utensils of the olive press.
chunks.basisNote: The names of the parts follow Bartenura.

words.note: A big log that presses down on the olives.

chunks.st: When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold
chunks.stMore: along with the olive press, even the movable utensils.

chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Someone who sells an olive press
chunks.st: One who sells an olive press
has sold the kora
chunks.stMore: as well, as it is the most fundamental element of the olive press.

summary: Someone who sells a bathhouse does not sell the boards, basins and curtains, unless he says everything inside is sold. Either way, he does not sell the water tanks or the wood storerooms.

chunks.st: One who sells a bathhouse
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.st: has not sold with it the boards that are placed on the floor,
nor has he sold the basins or the curtains [habilaniyot].
When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold along with the bathhouse.
Both in this case, where he executes the sale without specification, and in that
chunks.stMore: case, where he adds the phrase that he is selling everything that is in the bathhouse,

chunks.he: לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַמְּגֻרוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם
chunks.en: he has not sold the tanks of water
chunks.st: he has not sold the tanks of water,

chunks.en: and not the storerooms of wood.
chunks.st: nor has he sold the storerooms for wood,
chunks.stMore: as an explicit sales agreement is required for these matters.

summary: Someone who sells a city sells its houses, pits, bathhouses and other buildings, but not the things that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the city's guard is sold with it.

chunks.st: One who sells a city
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.st: has sold with it the houses,
the pits, the ditches and caves,
the bathhouses and the dovecotes,
and the olive presses and beit hashelaḥin, as will be explained in the Gemara,

chunks.en: but not the things that can be moved.
chunks.st: but he has not sold the movable property in the city.

chunks.en: But when he said to him,
chunks.st: But when the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: even if there were animals and servants in it,
chunks.st: even if there were cattle and Canaanite slaves in the city,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these entities are sold.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who sells a city
has sold with it the santar,
chunks.stMore: the meaning of which will be explained in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz leaves the word to the Gemara; Bartenura explains it as the city's guard.

summary: Someone who sells a field also sells the small things that belong to the field, like stones and reeds that are used there, the crops still growing, a small watch hut, and young trees.

chunks.st: One who sells a field
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has sold the stones that are used for it,
chunks.st: has sold the stones in the field that are for its use,

chunks.en: and the reeds in the vineyard that are used for it,
chunks.explain: Reeds that hold up the grapevines.
chunks.st: and the reeds in the vineyard that are for its use,

chunks.en: and the grain that is still attached to the ground,
chunks.st: and the produce that is still attached to the ground,
and the cluster of reeds

chunks.en: that is smaller than a beis rova,
chunks.st: that occupy less than the area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed [beit rova],

chunks.en: and the watch hut that is not made with clay,
chunks.st: and the watch station that is not plastered with clay,

chunks.en: and the carob tree that is not grafted,
chunks.st: and the young carob tree that has not yet been grafted,

words.note: A branch of another tree joined onto it.

chunks.st: and the untrimmed sycamore that is still young.

summary: The seller of a field does not sell things that are not part of the field, like detached crops or big separate things like a cistern or a dovecote. The Rabbis argue about buying a path to them, and they teach that a gift, a split between brothers, or hekdesh includes everything.

chunks.st: But he has not sold along with the field

chunks.en: the stones that are not used for it,
chunks.st: the stones that are not designated for use in the field,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הַקָּנִים שֶׁבַּכֶּרֶם שֶׁאֵינָן לְצָרְכּוֹ,
chunks.en: and not the reeds in the vineyard that are not used for it,
chunks.st: and not the reeds in the vineyard that are not designated for its use,
and not the produce

chunks.en: that is already cut from the ground.
chunks.st: that is already detached from the ground.
When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you
it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold along with the field.
Both in this case, where he executes the sale without specification, and in that
chunks.stMore: case, where he adds the phrase that he is selling everything that is in the field,

chunks.st: he has not sold

chunks.he: לֹא אֶת מְחִצַּת הַקָּנִים שֶׁהִיא בֵית רֹבַע,
chunks.en: a patch of reeds that is a beis rova,
chunks.st: the cluster of reeds that occupy a beit rova
chunks.stMore: or more, as they are considered a separate field,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הַשּׁוֹמֵרָה שֶׁהִיא עֲשׂוּיָה בְטִיט,
chunks.en: and not the watch hut that is made with clay,
chunks.st: and he has not sold the watch station that is plastered with clay,

chunks.en: and not the grafted carob tree,
chunks.st: and not the carob tree that has been grafted,
and not the sycamore trunk.
chunks.stMore: All of these entities are significant in their own right and have a status independent from that of the fields, and they are therefore not included in the sale of the field. In continuation of the previous mishna (68b) discussing one who sells a field, the mishna teaches that even if he says that he is selling it and everything that is in it, has sold

chunks.st: neither the cistern,
nor the winepress,
nor the dovecote,
whether it is abandoned or utilized,
chunks.stMore: as these items are not part of the field itself.

chunks.en: And the seller must buy himself a path.
chunks.st: And the seller must purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain to reach whatever remains his. This is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva,
chunks.stMore: who holds that one who sells, sells generously; therefore, whatever is not explicitly excluded from the sale is assumed to be sold, and it is presumed that the seller did not retain for himself the right to the path that he requires to access his property.

chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:
The seller need not
chunks.stMore: purchase a path through the buyer’s domain, as it is assumed that since the seller withholds these items for himself, he also reserves a path to reach them.

chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva concedes

chunks.en: that when he said to him, except for these,
chunks.st: that when the seller says to the buyer in the bill of sale that he is selling the field apart from these things, i.e., the cistern and the winepress,

chunks.en: he does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: he need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain. Since these items would have been excluded from the sale even if he had said nothing, it is assumed that he also meant to reserve for himself the right to access them.

chunks.en: If he sold them to someone else,
chunks.st: But if the seller kept the field but sold the cistern and winepress to another person,
Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: the buyer does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: The buyer need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the seller’s domain to reach what he has bought, since a seller sells generously.

chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he needs to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: He must purchase for himself a path through the seller’s domain.

chunks.en: When is this said? With one who sells.
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, that these items are excluded, said? It is said with regard to one who sells a field,

chunks.en: But one who gives a gift
chunks.st: but with regard to one who gives it away as a gift,
it is assumed that he gives all of it, including everything found in the field.

chunks.en: Brothers who split up what they got:
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to brothers who divide their father’s estate among themselves,
when they each acquire a field as part of their inheritance,
they acquire all of it,
chunks.stMore: including the items that would be excluded from a sale.

chunks.en: One who takes the property of a ger:
chunks.st: So too, with regard to one who takes possession of the property of a convert,
when he takes possession of a field,
he takes possession of all of it.

chunks.en: Someone who gives a field to hekdesh
chunks.st: One who consecrates a field

chunks.explain: Hekdesh means things given to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: has consecrated all of it.
Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Someone who gives a field to hekdesh
chunks.st: One who consecrates a field
has not consecrated any of the items that are ordinarily excluded from a sale except for

chunks.he: אֶת הֶחָרוּב הַמֻּרְכָּב וְאֶת סַדַּן הַשִּׁקְמָה:
chunks.en: the grafted carob tree and the sycamore trunk.
chunks.st: the grafted carob tree and the sycamore trunk.
